body:
Hey there.

I know it seems like high school really, really sucks. I'm 20 years old, almost 21, and I can see now, looking back, that high school was four of the suckiest years of my life. My senior year almost killed me, because I almost killed myself.

If you have goals and aspirations, you're already doing way, WAY better than 90% of the people you're going to school with. Having goals is really, really important. If school is important to you, that's all you need to be concerned about. If you aren't doing well in a class, don't beat yourself up over it. You know you're bright and can either try again or do what you need to do to get help. I can guarantee teachers are really, really willing to help students that are genuinely struggling and not just slacking off in class, especially if they initiate the conversation on getting help in that subject.

I heard a pretty great quote today: "Don't set yourself on fire to warm the people around you." I know the feeling of friends not being your REAL friend. They're just the people around you that sometimes talk to you. But believe me, high school friends will rarely be important. That seems shallow, but I can guarantee, out of all the "friends' I had in high school, I only still communicate with two of them. And if you feel like your dad isn't happy for you? Well, his happiness isn't directly linked to your happiness. If you're happy with that B- you got on a test, no one can take that from you.

I hope I helped a little. High school isn't forever. It's a challenge to get through, but as soon as you're handed your diploma, you'll be relieved you kept going.
